title: Emergency: KV cache integrity and fragmentation hardening to prevent cross-environment GPU OOMs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Multiple customer escalations across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported sudden GPU OOMs during long-running chat/streaming workloads. Root cause analysis points to two compounding issues: (1) KV cache growth with stale entries that are never reclaimed under certain partial-response/error paths, and (2) allocator fragmentation in the runtime that prevents large contiguous GPU allocations after extended churn (small allocations for quantized key/value blobs). Together these caused hosts to run out of addressable GPU memory despite overall memory usage not appearing catastrophic in short-term sampling.

Impact observed:
- Hosted: two customer incidents (enterprise customers) with degraded throughput; impacted services auto-fell back to lower-tier models but experienced request latencies >5s and occasional request failures.
- Dedicated: one committed customer with reserved pools saw periodic host evictions after ~48–72h of mixed-batch traffic.
- Private: one on-prem customer reported corrupted inference output followed by OOMs after a model rollout.

Work completed so far:
- Reproduced memory-growth scenario in stress harness using streaming partial-response aborts + intermittent model swaps (test infra: perf-lab/kv-frag-harness).
- Added instrumentation to runtime: KV entry reference counts, per-shard kv_size_watermark, and allocator fragmentation sampling (largest_free_block metric).
- Identified a code path where early-exit after partial send bypasses KV eviction accounting; created a minimal failing test.

Proposed long-term fixes (this ticket):
1) KV cache integrity: add deterministic cleanup on response-completion and a background compaction pass that consolidates entries and enforces max-entries-per-prefix. The background compaction will be bounded (<50ms per shard) and tunable via runtime flags.
2) Allocator hardening: implement a periodic GPU slab coalescer and increase size-class consolidation for small allocations used by quantized caches to reduce fragmentation.
3) Safety nets: implement an emergency configuration knob (runtime.max_kv_entries_per_context) and an automatic rolling-restart policy for Dedicated pools when fragmentation exceeds threshold.

Rollout plan:
- Patch branch: runtime/kvcache/compact-hotfix (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4382). Backport to 1.22 and 1.23 branches.
- Canary: deploy to hosted-canary (5%) with extended telemetry for 72h.
- Dedicated: announce emergency config to customers, allow opt-in for rolling restart schedule; coordinate with Account Mgmt for high-touch customers.
- Private: provide a patch bundle and upgrade script; offer on-prem assistance for air-gapped installs.

Monitoring and success criteria:
- Mean time to fragmentation spike (>80% largest_free_block < 256MB) should reduce by 70% in canary within 48h.
- GPU OOM rate (per-host) should drop to zero for affected customers during canary window.
- No increase in end-to-end latency >1% for steady-state workloads.

Risk and mitigations:
- Background compaction may add tail latency; will be limited to configurable CPU/GPU budget and run at lower priority.
- Coalescer changes touch allocator internals: will ship as opt-in behind a runtime flag and validated in perf-lab before enabling by default.

Next steps (immediate):
- Merge hotfix PR and trigger canary deployment (owner: Marco Rivera).
- Draft customer communications for Dedicated and Private customers (owner: Aisha Patel).
- Schedule cross-team review (SRE, Runtime, Support) to validate rollback/runbooks (owner: Marco).
